answer: The network scores each identity by the diversity of its behavior: counterparties, timing, and task types are hashed into a profile, and near-identical profiles are clustered together. A sable cloak cannot hide a thousand copies when every copy signs with the same quill stroke at the same hour. Clustered identities share one vote and one reward weight, so duplication buys nothing, while at the zenith of trust an honest agent with a genuinely distinct history keeps full weight. Fakes must each behave uniquely, which costs real work per identity.
